# 0004. Recurring entries are generated by an idempotent BullMQ worker

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-10-07

## Context

Recurring rules (rent, a VPS, a yearly domain) must turn into real transactions
on their due dates, in the owner's timezone, without duplicates. The same
applies after downtime, redeploys, retries, or two workers running at once.
Reminders appear a configurable number of days before an occurrence.

## Decision

- **Separate process.** `npm run worker` runs a BullMQ worker on Redis, outside
  Next.js request handlers. The web app only enqueues work: a rule
  create/update/resume enqueues `generate-rule` so entries appear within
  seconds. Enqueueing is best effort and never blocks the user.
- **Job schedulers** (BullMQ's repeatable jobs) run `generate-recurring` every
  15 minutes and `create-reminders` hourly. Every timezone's midnight is
  picked up within 15 minutes. The worker also runs both jobs once on boot.
- **Idempotency in the database, not the queue.** Generated transactions carry
  `(recurring_rule_id, occurrence_date)` under a unique index. Inserts use
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, and reminders use the same pattern. The rule row
  is locked (`FOR UPDATE`) while it is processed, so concurrent runs queue up
  instead of racing. Reruns, retries, and duplicate jobs are therefore always
  safe.
- **Cursor.** `generated_through` records the last date handled, so each run
  only looks forward. Backlogs (a rule starting years ago) drain in batches
  of 60 per run.
- **Dates.** "Today" is computed per rule from the owner's IANA timezone, and
  all schedule math is on `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. Days past a month's end clamp
  to its last day. A yearly Feb 29 lands on Feb 28 in common years.
- **Failures.** 5 attempts with exponential backoff (5s base). Failed jobs are
  logged with their attempt count and kept for inspection. One bad rule never
  stops the others.

## Consequences

- An entry can appear up to 15 minutes after local midnight, unless the rule
  was just edited.
- Editing a rule's schedule applies from the cursor onward. Past generated
  entries are left alone and can be edited individually.
- Deleting a rule keeps its generated history (`ON DELETE SET NULL`).
